blocks.content: The TRAI Amendment Act, 2000 bifurcated the regulatory and dispute settlement functions of TRAI by establishing the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT).

rows: Regulation of telecom services and tariff setting
Adjudication of disputes and appellate jurisdiction
Decisions appealable directly to the Supreme Court

items: TDSAT was created under the 2000 Amendment Act, NOT the original TRAI Act of 1997.
Appeals against TDSAT orders lie directly to the Supreme Court, bypassing High Courts.
TRAI recommendations on telecom licensing terms are advisory and not legally binding on the Government.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 2000 Amendment strictly separated the regulatory functions from adjudicatory functions in the Indian telecom sector.
Established the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) to resolve sector disputes.
Reconstituted TRAI to comprise a Chairperson, up to two full-time members, and up to two part-time members.
Divested quasi-judicial powers from TRAI to ensure independent regulatory governance.
Appeals against any decision or order of TDSAT lie exclusively with the Supreme Court of India.
